properties.name: McAllister's Mill complex (grist and saw mills with two dams), Rock Creek

sources.cite: Campbell, E., Treatment Philosophy: The 1863 Landscape, Gettysburg National Military Park (NPS, March 2004), ch. 2 Cultural Features: Farm Building Complexes
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: Two known dams on the battlefield were on Rock Creek, about 650 yards north of the Baltimore Pike, part of the McAllister Mill complex, built for grist and saw mills; this was the closest grist mill for most farmers on the 1863 battlefield.

sources.cite: OpenStreetMap contributors, building and historic tags in the Gettysburg battlefield bounding box (Overpass API extract, 19 Oct 2026); used for building names and as a cross-check of position
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: Named point at the mill site.

properties.method: Point = OSM named point at the mill site; error covers the whole complex.
properties.notes: The mill buildings, dams and lanes existed in 1863; only a site point is placed. NPS puts the two dams about 650 yd north of the Baltimore Pike while this OSM point is about 280 m from the Pike, so the extent of the complex is UNKNOWN and the error is set to 150 m. Individual buildings UNKNOWN.
properties.geometry_represents: site position, not a footprint

properties.name: Gettysburg borough building mass 1 (Warren plate)
properties.period_note: Standing at the 1868-69 survey; most borough blocks were built up before 1863 but individual buildings are not dated.

sources.cite: U.S. Army Office of the Chief of Engineers, Battle field of Gettysburg (Warren survey 1868-69, reduced to 1 inch = 1000 ft, no troop positions), scan cw0353500
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: Solid building symbols along the street fronts of the borough as surveyed in 1868-69; letters W/B/S mark wood, brick, stone where drawn.

properties.method: Outline of an inked building mass on the Warren plate (cw0353500 registered to the cw0325000a frame), extracted by thresholding and contour tracing, then carried to ground coordinates through the global thin-plate-spline georeference. The plate draws buildings as solid symbols that are larger than the buildings and run together along the street fronts: this polygon is the extent of the ink, NOT an individual building footprint.
properties.notes: Buildings erected between July 1863 and 1869 cannot be separated from those standing in July 1863 using this plate alone.
properties.geometry_represents: extent of drawn building symbols (merges neighbouring buildings)
properties.georef_model: Bachelder 1876 / Warren 1868-69 plate georeferenced by a thin-plate spline fitted to 86 control points (surviving buildings, road junctions, bridges, summits); leave-one-out error median 9.9 m, 90th percentile 22.0 m, maximum 32 m (evidence/gcps_final.json)

sources.cite: U.S. Army Office of the Chief of Engineers, Battle field of Gettysburg (Warren survey 1868-69, reduced to 1 inch = 1000 ft, no troop positions), scan cw0353500
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: Solid building symbols along the street fronts of the borough as surveyed in 1868-69; letters W/B/S mark wood, brick, stone where drawn.

properties.method: Outline of an inked building mass on the Warren plate (cw0353500 registered to the cw0325000a frame), extracted by thresholding and contour tracing, then carried to ground coordinates through the global thin-plate-spline georeference. The plate draws buildings as solid symbols that are larger than the buildings and run together along the street fronts: this polygon is the extent of the ink, NOT an individual building footprint.
properties.notes: Buildings erected between July 1863 and 1869 cannot be separated from those standing in July 1863 using this plate alone.
properties.geometry_represents: extent of drawn building symbols (merges neighbouring buildings)
properties.georef_model: Bachelder 1876 / Warren 1868-69 plate georeferenced by a thin-plate spline fitted to 86 control points (surviving buildings, road junctions, bridges, summits); leave-one-out error median 9.9 m, 90th percentile 22.0 m, maximum 32 m (evidence/gcps_final.json)
